name: Van Hanh
role: Celebrated monk of Cổ Pháp, teacher of Lý Công Uẩn and a voice in the 1009 succession.
known_facts: A famous monk of Cổ Pháp pagoda, in what is now Bắc Ninh.
Traditionally credited with teaching and advising the young Lý Công Uẩn.
Said in the annals to have counselled the Early Lê kings before the rise of the Lý.
Reported to have argued in 1009 that the country needed an adult ruler.
Died around 1018 and was honoured by the Lý court.
interpretation: A spare Vietnamese monk of about seventy, short and slightly stooped, close-shaven head with faint grey stubble, deep-lined face, calm lowered eyes, thin lips. He wears a faded ochre-brown robe of coarse cloth over a darker under-robe, a brown wooden rosary around his neck, and a folded palm-leaf fan tucked into his sash.
